detail.body:
Selected Linear and AutoEP GroupedExperts train with HiFloat8 through one public TorchAO `quantize_` call. AO now owns both configuration types and both registered handlers; DeepSpeed selects modules and manages training lifecycle without defining a grouped quantization handler or choosing a GEMM callable.

[RFC #8777](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/issues/8777) documents the architecture, quick start and historical compute/end-to-end comparisons.

Implementation:

- `HiFloat8GroupedConfig` and the existing Linear recipe derive from AO's shared `HiFloat8Config`. Grouped uses the inherited 15/15/224 defaults and `from_dict` validation. Legacy `HiFloat8LinearConfig` native-range defaults remain compatible. No nested policy wrapper is added.
- Engine parses the same numerical JSON into the applicable immutable recipes, checks native/lifecycle capabilities before any conversion, builds one `ModuleFqnToConfig` map and calls `quantize_` after AutoEP/device preparation and before optimizer creation.
- AO's grouped handler accepts a module exposing the existing `grouped_mm` slot and binds the unchanged HiFloat8 grouped functional/autograd implementation. It imports no DeepSpeed container. The former `deepspeed/runtime/torchao.py` adapter is removed.
- The accelerator lazily resolves public `torchao.hifloat8` configuration/probe APIs. Dense-only selection does not require grouped exports; selected experts require `HiFloat8GroupedConfig` before conversion. There is no DeepSpeed reference to `hifloat8_grouped_mm` for execution.
- Native BF16/FP16 grouped GEMM remains in `deepspeed/ops/npu`, independent of AO. DeepSpeed retains routing, padding, activation, communication, parameter/state identity and caller-facing dtype.
- Qwen3.5 text-wrapper/checkpoint fixes and NPU permutation generation remain in this PR as separate functional commits.

Merge this fragment into the existing training configuration and use the normal `deepspeed.initialize(..., config=ds_config)` call:

```json
{
  "bf16": {"enabled": true},
  "zero_optimization": {"stage": 2},
  "hifloat8": {
    "enabled": true,
    "backend": "torchao",
    "module_name_patterns": ["*.experts", "*.shared_experts.*_proj"],
    "min_numel": 65536
  }
}
```

Install the paired sources with `torchao>=0.18,<0.19`, matching Torch/TorchNPU and CANN, and automatic activation enabled. No explicit `import torchao_npu` is needed. AutoEP topology, optimizer/batch settings and trainable-parameter selection remain separate. See the [tutorial](https://github.com/hazelduan/DeepSpeed/blob/95dd780ce4e2f534b484610f273d3ef21c505baf/docs/_tutorials/hifloat8_training.md).

October 19 validation on Ascend950PR, original Conda Python3.11.15, Torch/TorchNPU2.11.0, TorchAO0.18.0, CANN9.1.0 and driver25.7.rc1:

- AO HiFloat8/namespace suites: **71 passed, 1 empty-Dense native-contract skip**. DeepSpeed focused suites: **342 passed, 32 CUDA-only skips**, including CPU reference cases.
- A fresh process imports `torch` and public `torchao` APIs, converts a Linear and a plain grouped module together, and runs native forward/backward. There is no explicit `torchao_npu` import and no DeepSpeed module loaded. The grouped configuration derives from `HiFloat8Config`.
- Actual AutoEP EP2/ZeRO-2: paired 30-step runs plus a reverse-order 100-step pair in each precision, BF16 and HiFloat8 separately. Inputs, losses, gradient norms and all **19 final tensors per rank are exact** against the previous paired DS/AO sources. Two layers/four experts, hidden64/intermediate128, batch1/sequence16, seed42 and rank-dependent data seed123+rank, AdamW1e-3, same CPU affinity. This is a small actual AutoEP model, not a full Qwen convergence run.
- NPU allocation peaks are identical before/after: **17,627,648 bytes initialization; 1,035,863,040 bytes training**. Initial 30-step P50 changes were BF16 +14.57%, HiFloat8 +1.05%; the reverse-order 100-step changes were BF16 −0.50%, HiFloat8 +0.45%. Ordinary BF16 execution code is unchanged. The samples show timing sensitivity and do not establish a stable speedup or regression.
- DP2/ZeRO-2/GAS2 checkpoint/resume retains exact subsequent losses, parameters and optimizer state. Typed Linear/grouped recipes have equal numerical fields; grouped modules reuse the same grouped recipe. Experts are replicated, so this is not AutoEP checkpoint proof.
- Local CPU focused tests: **40 passed, 82 NPU-dependent skips**. The first three reconstructed DeepSpeed commits were also tested independently: 199/6, 6/24 and 10/37 passed/skipped. Changed-file checks cover the full feature diff. Final trees match the validated source, with only a separately checked documentation wording correction after the initial native suites.

The previous published source pair was DS `6b91ff09` / AO `9c6dfb4`. Reproduction: `/data/dxq/hif8_a5_20260914/experiments/ao_grouped_handler_20261019_01` (`run_all.sh`, `postchecks.sh`, source manifests, exact configs/rank tables, per-rank results and comparisons). Original packages and host permissions were preserved; device access uses a task-local non-root container identity and cache paths.

The existing feature histories are consolidated by responsibility, preserving the final trees. No new PR was created.

- [`9a87125d`](https://github.com/hazelduan/DeepSpeed/commit/9a87125d42b170a511556eb1d21cff31697b79ce) — feat(npu): expose native grouped GEMM through accelerator capabilities

- [`95dd780c`](https://github.com/hazelduan/DeepSpeed/commit/95dd780ce4e2f534b484610f273d3ef21c505baf) — feat(hifloat8): integrate AO-owned quantize_ training handlers

- [`ea917fd`](https://gitcode.com/hazeldxq/torchao_npu/commit/ea917fd6a3fe72b9958feedaad4f0f11c5c50a27) — feat(ops): add differentiable native NPU grouped GEMM
- [`a388ef3`](https://gitcode.com/hazeldxq/torchao_npu/commit/a388ef388e945540fd4ef66a098f3d3d482ba4bb) — feat(hifloat8): register Linear and grouped training workflows
- [`e0d59bd`](https://gitcode.com/hazeldxq/torchao_npu/commit/e0d59bdfcc17721fb13e3cc4b6c949391d68aa7d) — bench(hifloat8): separate timing, memory and kernel attribution

Current sources: DeepSpeed [`95dd780c`](https://github.com/hazelduan/DeepSpeed/commit/95dd780ce4e2f534b484610f273d3ef21c505baf), AO [`e0d59bd`](https://gitcode.com/hazeldxq/torchao_npu/commit/e0d59bdfcc17721fb13e3cc4b6c949391d68aa7d) ([MR31](https://gitcode.com/Ascend/torchao_npu/merge_requests/31)), Swift [`3e9994baf`](https://github.com/hazelduan/ms-swift/commit/3e9994baf135f939dffefc9ad4773bae35e2b5b9). Swift changes are documentation only. Draft boundaries remain BF16 parameters/ZeRO0–2 on NPU; reject ZeRO3, pipeline, AutoTP/custom MPU, explicit MoE and fused gate/up overrides. Full-parameter convergence, LoRA, AutoEP checkpoint recovery, quantized checkpoint ingestion, offload/compile, EP8, multi-node and CUDA low precision remain outside the established support.

+# DeepSpeed Team
+title: "TorchAO HiFloat8 training"
+---
+
+DeepSpeed selects ordinary Linear and AutoEP GroupedExperts modules, probes the
+active accelerator's optional HiFloat8 APIs, and converts both kinds through one
+public `torchao.quantization.quantize_` call. DeepSpeed owns selection, activation,
+routing/padding, communication, optimizer and checkpoint lifecycle. TorchAO owns
+numerical policy and the quantization/GEMM implementations.
+
+## Quick start
+
+Add the following section to your existing DeepSpeed training configuration.
+AutoEP topology, batch size and optimizer settings remain in that configuration.
+
+```json
+{
+  "bf16": {"enabled": true},
+  "zero_optimization": {"stage": 2},
+  "hifloat8": {
+    "enabled": true,
+    "backend": "torchao",
+    "module_name_patterns": ["*.experts", "*.shared_experts.*_proj"],
+    "min_numel": 65536
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Pass the configuration to the normal initialization call; DeepSpeed applies
+HiFloat8 after AutoEP replacement and device placement, before optimizer setup:
+
+```python
+import deepspeed
+
+engine, optimizer, _, _ = deepspeed.initialize(
+    model=model,
+    model_parameters=model.parameters(),
+    config=ds_config,
+)
+```
+
+For a Dense-only model, omit AutoEP and select the actual Linear module names.
+Set `hifloat8.enabled=false` to return to the high-precision path.
+
+AutoEP topology and trainable-parameter selection are configured separately.
+Every pattern must match an eligible module. Optional `expected_module_count`
+checks the complete selection before backend loading. The existing schema is
+retained; legacy `backend="torchao_npu"` normalizes to `"torchao"`. The former
+`torch_npu` training-helper backend and the temporary `low_precision` section are
+rejected with a migration instruction.
+
+## Conversion and device ownership
+
+`DeepSpeedAccelerator.get_hifloat8_provider()` defaults to `None`. The NPU
+implementation lazily returns the public `torchao.hifloat8` APIs after checking
+optional dependency/version availability. Unsupported accelerators fail before
+conversion. No NPU import or device-specific kernel selection occurs in Engine.
+
+`ModuleFqnToConfig` maps selected Linear modules to `HiFloat8Config` and selected
+experts to AO's `HiFloat8GroupedConfig`. Both parse the same numerical settings
+through their common `HiFloat8Config` base. Each recipe is immutable and reused
+across its selected modules; no nested policy wrapper is needed.
+Both handlers are registered by AO. The grouped handler binds AO's existing GEMM
+through the module's `grouped_mm` slot; it does not import a DeepSpeed container.
+Engine selects configurations and calls `quantize_`, without defining a handler
+or selecting a grouped function. Both preserve Parameter identity, names, metadata, `requires_grad`,
+mode and state-dict keys. There is no second model-conversion API or registry.
+The expert container remains owned by DeepSpeed and retains its activation and
+routing/padding behavior.
+
+The separate `get_grouped_mm()` accelerator hook supplies ordinary high-precision
+GEMM. Its NPU implementation calls TorchNPU with explicit list-input autograd,
+packed `[E,N,K]` weights and empty-group gradients. The operator implementation
+lives in `deepspeed/ops/npu/grouped_mm.py`; the accelerator only resolves the
+capability. HiFloat8 API discovery lives in `accelerator/npu/hifloat8.py`.
+BF16/FP16 grouped training does not require TorchAO. CPU/CUDA dispatch retains
+its existing implementation.
+
+## Optional TorchAO policy
+
+Install `torchao>=0.18,<0.19` and the paired Ascend extension with public HiFloat8
+policy/probe APIs and registered handlers. Selected experts additionally require
+`HiFloat8GroupedConfig`; Dense-only selection does not require grouped exports.
+With the extension's automatic activation enabled, DeepSpeed imports
+`torchao.hifloat8`; users do not need to import `torchao_npu` or convert the model
+manually. Upstream TorchAO alone does not provide this HiFloat8 implementation.
+Missing APIs, versions,
+invalid policy or unavailable requested forward/dX/dW kernels fail before
+conversion; policy parsing uses `HiFloat8Config.from_dict`.
+
+Missing, null or empty `config` uses the established input/weight/gradient scale
+denominators `15/15/224`. Explicit overrides remain supported. `compute_dtype`
+selects high-precision staging and GEMM output precision (`null`, `"bfloat16"`
+or `"float16"`); operands remain HiFloat8 payloads and accumulation is
+kernel-owned. Converted Linear and expert modules return their caller's dtype,
+so FP16 working GEMMs compose with BF16 residuals. Raw tensor helpers retain
+their working/output dtype contract. Scaling currently supports per-tensor only.
+
+## Validation boundary
+
+The current NPU HiFloat8 path requires BF16 model parameters and accepts ZeRO
+stages 0–2. ZeRO-3, PipelineModule, AutoTP, custom MPU and explicit DeepSpeed MoE
+layers are rejected, as is an explicit fused gate/up override on selected experts.
+Quantized checkpoint ingestion into ZeRO-3 is unsupported;
+checkpoints retain high-precision weights and their original state names.
+Reconstruct the same policy for resume. The opt-in DP2/GAS2 lifecycle entry point
+is `tests/unit/runtime/hifloat8_resume_validation.py`, whose experts are replicated.
+It does not establish AutoEP checkpoint recovery.
+
+The integration includes Qwen3.5 text-wrapper routing compatibility and NPU
+permutation index generation. These reuse AutoEP's existing preset and kernel
+extension points without adding HiFloat8 configuration. Full-parameter convergence,
+LoRA, offload, compile, EP8, multi-node and CUDA low-precision hardware validation
+remain separate gates.

+    if isinstance(value, dict):

+    if isinstance(value, tuple):
+        return tuple(snapshot(v) for v in value)
+    if isinstance(value, list):
+        return [snapshot(v) for v in value]
+    return copy.deepcopy(value)

+        compare_nested(vars(a), vars(b))
+    elif isinstance(a, dict):

+    elif isinstance(a, (tuple, list)):
